scores.evidence: Same-engine CDC is far more reliable, and an engine change on top of a migration compounds risk.
scores.rationale: Mechanisms (CDC, reverse CDC, write-hold, read-your-writes, NIST 800-88) are accurate; minor imprecision such as reverse CDC on managed DBs and 'zero data loss' claims, and replicated-replica read-only via SELECT grants, have no major consequence.

scores.evidence: Worst failure: Split-brain writes. On-prem and cloud both accept bookings during cutover, which causes double-booked OR or clinic slots
scores.rationale: Solves the real problem, defines 'no downtime' sensibly as a short held-write pause, is buildable, and defers scope explicitly with reasons; vendor-licensing check is only a pre-assumption.

scores.evidence: CP, one writer. Exactly one database is authoritative at any moment. No dual-writes, no multi-master.
scores.rationale: Single-writer principle, write-authority flag, proxy indirection, and singleton guard are applied consistently across all phases with no notable contradictions.

scores.evidence: At least 3 full rehearsals and at least 1 full rollback rehearsal on a staging environment built from IaC, using a masked clone
scores.rationale: Validation targets specific risks (shadow diff, reconciliation, dry-run message match, load test at 2x peak, rollback rehearsal) with checkable criteria, early slice, and post-cutover continuous monitoring; some thresholds are invented but mostly labeled as targets.

scores.evidence: Assumptions to confirm before Phase 0: Vendor product? If the system is a vendor product such as Epic Cadence
scores.rationale: Key assumptions and revisit triggers are stated and RTO/RPO flagged as to-confirm, but scale, team size and budget are not stated, and many thresholds (30 s, 5 s) appear without basis.

scores.evidence: outbound feeds firing twice, which sends duplicate SMS reminders to patients and duplicate SIU messages to the EHR.
scores.rationale: Covers split-brain, duplicate outbound sends, stale reads, missed consumers, CDC lag, DLQs, rollback triggers, and PHI incident tabletop with concrete detection and recovery; adversarial input is thinner.

scores.evidence: Infra and app deploy from Terraform/Bicep through a CI pipeline. Nothing is set up by hand.
scores.rationale: Deployment as code, dashboards, alerts, on-call, war-room, and rollback are concrete, but ownership/team sizing and runbook staffing are not detailed.

scores.evidence: Revisit after migration only if licensing cost is over budget.
scores.rationale: Build vs buy is noted and cost dashboards appear, but there is no estimate of dual-running costs, egress, circuits, or 30–90 day standby, and no cost controls.

scores.evidence: Flip to rehost (lift-and-shift VMs) if licensing or OS dependencies block managed services. Re-architecting is deferred (§7).
scores.rationale: Decisions table lists revisit triggers, indirection via proxy/DNS, same-engine choice, rollback via reverse CDC, and deferred one-way changes with pull-forward conditions.
Scope is held to replatform with explicit deferrals; some ceremony (AI N/A rows, 3 rehearsals, 14-day gates, pen test) and the all-phase table add weight but are mostly domain-justified.

scores.evidence: Tasks, executed from the rehearsed script: 1. The proxy holds writes, with a bounded queue. 2. Confirm CDC lag is 0 and checksums match.
scores.rationale: Dependency-ordered phases, concrete first slice, per-phase exit checks, and revisit triggers let a team start immediately.

checklist.evidence: BAA signed; landing-zone policy guardrails; private endpoints only; CMK encryption; TLS 1.2+; AD federation; read-only DB login
list every reader and writer: ADT inbound, SIU outbound, reminder/IVR vendor, billing, reporting/BI, and ODBC links from Access or Excel
hourly row counts plus per-table checksums, and a nightly full-hash comparison of the appointment and slot tables.
A single flag says which side is authoritative. Every outbound interface and batch job ... checks it before acting
The rollback rehearsal restores on-prem authority in under 15 min with zero data loss.
Redundant private link: ExpressRoute or Direct Connect, plus a backup IPsec VPN
The DR failover test meets RTO ≤ 1 h and RPO ≤ 5 min (targets to confirm with clinical ops).
Federate to the existing hospital AD (Entra ID / SAML). No new user store.
Load-test the cloud at 2× the observed peak, for example the Monday 08:00 booking surge.
Choose a low-volume window (e.g. Sunday 02:00, avoiding month-end and holidays).
Decommission with NIST 800-88 media sanitization certificates.

traps.evidence: Hold a 4-hour war-room watch, then a 72 h heightened watch.
staging environment built from IaC, using a masked clone of production data
Dependency inventory ... ADT inbound, SIU outbound, reminder/IVR vendor, billing, reporting/BI
Replatform. Same app code on cloud VMs or containers ... No refactoring during the move.

note: Strong, coherent single-writer migration plan with staged reads, rehearsed rollback, and interface handling; weak on cost, team sizing, break-glass, and clinical cutover communication/hypercare detail.
